newsitem.title: USA: Southern Co. says cool weather depressed earnings.
newsitem.headline: Southern Co. says cool weather depressed earnings.

text.p: Southern Co. said Thursday that earnings fell 25 percent in the second quarter because cool weather in the Southeast spurred consumers and businesses to keep air conditioners off, depressing demand for electricity.

The company, the largest producer of electricity in the United States, said net income fell to $215 million, or 31 cents a share, in the quarter, from $287 million, or 43 cents a share, a year earlier. Sales rose 6 percent to $2.72 billion from $2.56 billion.
The results came in below expectations on Wall Street, where analysts had forecast earnings of 40 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks estimates.

"The unusually cool weather throughout our southeastern territory caused a decrease in demand responsible for the vast majority of the decline in earnings," Chairman A.W. Dahlberg said in a statement.
Electricity use by consumers fell 3.2 percent in the first half of 1997 and consumption by offices, stores and other companies fell 1.1 percent, the company said. But industrial use rose 2.1 percent.
Total sales of electricity to customers, including other utilities, fell 3.1 percent to 71.8 billion kilowatt-hours in the first half, it said.

Southern, based in Atlanta, is the parent firm of Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Gulf Power, Mississippi Power and Savannah Electric. It also has operations overseas and provides marketing, trading and technical services.
Southern stock fell 12.5 cents to $21.375 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
